teaching.hint: How large must at least one sorted gap be between the minimum and maximum?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The average-gap lower bound lets buckets be narrow enough that the maximum sorted gap cannot be hidden within one bucket.
solution_outline.approach: Find the minimum and maximum. Partition their range into at most `n` equal-width buckets using the ceiling average gap; keep the minimum and maximum of each nonempty bucket, then compare consecutive nonempty buckets.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A bucket contains only its two extremes; its width is below the guaranteed maximum-gap lower bound. The scan remembers the maximum of the preceding nonempty bucket.
solution_outline.correctness: At least one of the `n-1` sorted gaps reaches the ceiling average. Every intra-bucket gap is smaller, so the true maximum is a boundary gap between consecutive nonempty buckets, all of which are checked.
solution_outline.pitfall: When all values equal, the range is zero and bucket width would otherwise be zero.

common_wrong_turns: Sorting despite the required linear bound
Using a zero width for equal values
Comparing only adjacent occupied bucket indices
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; retained the mandatory complexity bound, duplicates, and full value range.
